    10	def fit_wealth_quantile(df: pd.DataFrame, q: float, year: int = 1996) -> dict:
    11	    """Linear quantile regression of composite_wealth_<year> on race, sex and
    12	    ever_jailed at quantile q.
    13	
    14	    Returns {"coef": {"intercept", "black", "hispanic", "male", "ever_jailed"}, "n"}.
    15	    """
    16	    if not 0 < q < 1:
    17	        raise ValueError("q must be strictly between 0 and 1")
    18	
    19	    outcome = f"composite_wealth_{year}"
    20	    if outcome not in df.columns:
    21	        raise KeyError(outcome)
    22	
    23	    # The design uses white/female as the omitted categories.  The source
    24	    # data spells Hispanic as ``hipanic``; retain that spelling here while
    25	    # naming the resulting coefficient conventionally.
    26	    x = np.column_stack(
    27	        (
    28	            np.ones(len(df)),
    29	            (df["race"].to_numpy() == "black").astype(float),
    30	            (df["race"].to_numpy() == "hipanic").astype(float),
    31	            (df["sex"].to_numpy() == "male").astype(float),
    32	            df["ever_jailed"].to_numpy(dtype=float),
    33	        )
    34	    )
    35	    y = df[outcome].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    36	    n = len(y)
    37	
    38	    # For residual r = y - Xb, write r = r_plus - r_minus with both parts
    39	    # nonnegative.  Minimizing q*r_plus + (1-q)*r_minus is exactly the
    40	    # quantile check loss.  Sparse identity blocks avoid constructing a
    41	    # dense n by (2*n) constraint matrix.
    42	    constraints = hstack((x, eye(n, format="csr"), -eye(n, format="csr")), format="csr")
    43	    objective = np.r_[np.zeros(5), np.full(n, q), np.full(n, 1.0 - q)]
    44	    result = linprog(
    45	        objective,
    46	        A_eq=constraints,
    47	        b_eq=y,
    48	        bounds=[(None, None)] * 5 + [(0, None)] * (2 * n),
    49	        method="highs",
    50	    )
    51	    if not result.success:
    52	        raise RuntimeError(f"quantile regression failed: {result.message}")
    53	
    54	    coefficients = result.x[:5]

    58	                ("intercept", "black", "hispanic", "male", "ever_jailed"),
    59	                coefficients.tolist(),
    60	            )
    61	        ),

    63	    }
